title: Vilnius - capital of Lithuania
snippet: Vilnius is the capital of Lithuania and its largest city, sitting at the confluence of the Neris and Vilnia rivers.
content: Vilnius is the capital of Lithuania and its largest city. It lies in the southeast of the country where the Neris and Vilnia rivers meet. The Old Town of Vilnius is one of the largest surviving medieval old towns in Northern Europe and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: History of Vilnius - founding and Gediminas
snippet: Vilnius was first mentioned in written sources in 1323, in letters of Grand Duke Gediminas inviting merchants and craftsmen to the city.
content: The name Vilnius was first recorded in 1323 in letters written by Grand Duke Gediminas, who invited German merchants, craftsmen, and Jews to settle in the new capital of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

title: The Neris river through Vilnius
snippet: The Neris is the river that flows through Vilnius; the smaller Vilnia river gave the city its name.
content: The Neris river flows through the centre of Vilnius. The much smaller Vilnia river, a tributary of the Neris, is generally credited with giving the city its name.

title: Weather and climate of Vilnius
snippet: Vilnius has a humid continental climate with warm summers; July is typically the warmest month.
content: Vilnius has a humid continental climate. Summers are warm and moderately wet, with July usually the warmest month. Winters are cold with frequent snow.

title: Old Town of Vilnius - UNESCO World Heritage
snippet: The historic centre of Vilnius was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1994.
content: The historic centre (Old Town) of Vilnius was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1994 for its Gothic, Renaissance, Baroque, and Classical architecture.

title: Lithuania - country profile
snippet: Lithuania is a country in the Baltic region of Europe; its capital is Vilnius.
content: Lithuania is one of the three Baltic states in northern Europe. Its capital and largest city is Vilnius. Lithuania is a member of the European Union and NATO.

title: Getting around Vilnius - travel guide
snippet: A practical guide to public transport, neighbourhoods, and day trips from Vilnius.
content: Vilnius has an extensive bus and trolleybus network. Popular day trips include Trakai castle and the Hill of Crosses.

title: Universities in Vilnius
snippet: Vilnius University, founded in 1579, is one of the oldest universities in Northern and Eastern Europe.
content: Vilnius University was founded in 1579 and is among the oldest universities in this part of Europe. It anchors a lively student population in the city.

title: Baltic capitals compared: Vilnius, Riga, Tallinn
snippet: How the three Baltic capital cities differ in size, history, and character.
content: Vilnius, Riga, and Tallinn are the capitals of Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia respectively. Vilnius is the southernmost and most inland of the three.

title: Best time to visit Lithuania
snippet: Summer, especially June to August, is the most popular time to visit Lithuania.
content: The most popular time to visit Lithuania is summer, from June to August, when days are long and temperatures are pleasant.

title: Cuisine of Vilnius
snippet: Traditional dishes you will find in Vilnius, from cepelinai to cold beet soup.
content: Vilnius cuisine features hearty dishes such as cepelinai (potato dumplings) and saltibarsciai, a bright pink cold beet soup served in summer.

title: Population of Vilnius
snippet: Vilnius is the most populous city in Lithuania, with roughly half a million residents.
content: Vilnius is the largest city in Lithuania by population, home to around 580,000 residents in the city proper.

title: Rivers of Lithuania
snippet: The Nemunas is the longest river in Lithuania; the Neris is a major tributary passing through Vilnius.
content: The Nemunas is the longest river in Lithuania. The Neris, which flows through Vilnius, is one of its largest tributaries.

title: Vilnius Old Town walking routes
snippet: Suggested walking routes through the cobbled streets of the Vilnius Old Town.
content: Walking routes through the Vilnius Old Town typically start at the Cathedral Square and wind past Gediminas Tower and the Gates of Dawn.

title: Climate data for Baltic cities
snippet: Average monthly temperatures and rainfall for major Baltic cities.
content: Average July highs in the Baltic capitals hover in the low-to-mid twenties Celsius, with Vilnius among the warmest owing to its inland position.
